item.title: Operations as a System of Power and Dependence
item.lead: The operational analysis culminates in a question of power: who controls the account, data, contract, and access to the user?

blocks.text: The dossier describes a model in which agencies manage login credentials, account rights, and revenue streams. As a result, the creator can become dependent on an organization that simultaneously controls marketing, customer contact, technology, and payment. In the source, this is referred to as the legal or digital hostage loop.

On the user side, a comparable asymmetry arises: the creator or their representation sees the CRM profile and sales data, while the buyer does not always see who the conversation partner truly is, what information has been stored, or for how long that information will persist. According to the dossier, the operational layer thus creates an asymmetrical distribution of knowledge.

For a forensic investigation, this means that an organizational chart can be more important than a single incident. Who holds the accounts? Who has access to CRM? Who determines scripts? Who can block payments? Who manages content? Who can terminate contracts? The answers reveal the true chain.

The core is therefore not only how a chat is conducted, but how labor, data, identity, and money are organizationally linked. This is the background that the seven-part series attempts to make visible.
